page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture. The compute configuration delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 processor-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM allocated per core. The server operates with zero attached GPU hardware accelerators.

Storage functionality on this instance relies exclusively on network-attached block volumes, as no local NVMe or SSD storage devices are physically bundled. In addition, the configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires network administrators to configure external routing, Cloud NAT, or assign ephemeral or static external IPs when public internet access is required.

By utilizing dedicated Arm cores, the instance provides power-efficient compute capacity and consistent hardware resource isolation without shared-core throttling. Cost efficiency is driven by the resource density of the Arm platform, providing an effective hardware footprint for workloads compiled to target arm64 binaries.

The n4a-standard-8 is designed for workloads requiring a balanced allocation of processing threads and memory capacity without needing high local storage IOPS. Common deployment targets include containerized web applications, microservices backends, API gateways, enterprise middleware, and continuous integration runners executing on Arm environments.
